posts.title: Is Time Really a Stubbornly Persistent Illusion?
posts.description: Einstein showed that two observers moving past each other disagree about which distant events happen at the same time, and many have concluded that there is no real “now”. But the light left over from the early universe tells a different story: it defines one cosmic time and one state of rest across the whole universe, and with them an objective present.

posts.title: Why does the universe expand?
posts.description: A story about the main reasons I now think the universe expands because collapsed matter must continue as an expanding cosmology, the expansion is the collapse read from the other side, and the rate is fixed by the cosmological constant alone.

posts.title: The Universe: from an antimatter black hole
posts.description: A friend's question about an Eddington–Finkelstein diagram sent me looking for a better explanation, and I found a cycloid. Eighteen papers later, here is what came of it: horizons that are not places, a universe with a real now, three generations that are counted rather than chosen, and black holes that become universes. None of it asks to be taken on faith.
